title: AI/ML Ops Factory
valueStatement: Factory that generates governed ML project repositories with Terraform infrastructure, CI/CD, and honest evidence about what has actually been run.
architectureHighlight: Shared local-to-cloud lifecycle with conditional registration — local green does not claim Azure lineage.
description: An Azure-first factory that generates governed ML project repositories: Terraform infrastructure, a shared local-to-cloud lifecycle, conditional registration, and evidence that stays honest about what has actually been run.
pitch: Factory that generates governed ML project repositories with Terraform infrastructure, CI/CD, and honest evidence about what has actually been run.
challenge: Enterprise MLOps usually collapses into a notebook, a portal click, or a generator that pretends Databricks, Foundry, and Azure ML are one lifecycle. The factory had to generate self-contained project repos without importing a taxi demo as the platform, and without claiming live Azure proof from local tests.
development: Re-engineered the Azure MLOps v2 accelerator idea into AIML-SCAFFOLD: manifest in, deterministic generate, doctor the result. Proven reference is azure-mlops (taxi fare, Dev and Prod infra, registered model, working batch endpoints). Shared lifecycle is prepare → train → evaluate → conditionally register → explicit-version batch serve. Terraform is the R1 Azure IaC. Foundry, Databricks retrieval, and agent runtime stay on the roadmap until they have their own evidence.
outcome: A generator plus a live reference: AIML-SCAFFOLD produces the project; azure-mlops is the taxi instance that actually trained, registered, and served. This portfolio hosts the architecture write-up, not a fake factory UI. Sources: AIML-SCAFFOLD and azure-mlops.

gallery.title: Factory control plane
gallery.description: Intake through monitoring on one wall: pipeline health, registry, drift alerts, and the 3D factory the generator is supposed to instantiate — not a screenshot of a portal

journey.title: Do not turn the taxi into the platform
journey.description: Kept AIML-SCAFFOLD as contracts, generator, templates, and policy. azure-mlops remains the proven Azure ML reference. Generated repos are product-specific.

journey.title: Same code locally and in Azure ML
journey.description: Dev defaults to local execution of prepare / train / evaluate / promotion / score. Azure compute is an explicit opt-in with a one-node Dev ceiling — local proof does not claim cloud lineage.

journey.title: Terraform as the R1 deploy path
journey.description: Preserved the proven Terraform Azure ML route (keyless storage, Key Vault, Log Analytics, scale-to-zero, Entra/OIDC). Bicep stays reference, not a silent rewrite of working apply.

journey.title: Identity and evidence as the product
journey.description: Factory identities cannot be inherited by generated workloads. Every mutation goes through saved-plan digest review. Unproven Foundry/agent work is labeled unproven.

specs.title: Deterministic project generator
specs.description: Manifest → validate → plan → generate → doctor. Source-manifest, resolved-plan, and generation-receipt are the provenance, not a wiki page written after the fact.

specs.title: Local-first, cloud-honest lifecycle
specs.description: The same Python modules run locally and as a four-stage Azure ML pipeline. Local green does not register as Azure ML execution, lineage, or endpoint health.

specs.title: Conditional register and explicit versions
specs.description: Evaluate can refuse to register. Batch serving pins an explicit model version. Champion/challenger is a gate, not a dashboard color.

specs.title: Split identities, digest-bound apply
specs.description: Generated projects do not inherit platform-admin privileges. Destructive ACR ownership drift was caught before apply. Portal clicks are not the change process.

specs.title: Reference instance that actually ran
specs.description: azure-mlops: Dev and Prod resource groups, registered taxi-model, working batch endpoints. Microsoft template bugs (OIDC id-token, conda setuptools, SKU) were fixed in the forks so the next project inherits them.
